blocks.text: Direction for this wave

content.value: THE FINISHED EXPERIENCE: A user who already runs a standalone box (self-serving its own content over its own Caddy/TLS) OPTIONALLY pastes a Cloudflare API token (bp provider add cloudflare, already shipped) and then runs ONE verb to put a custom domain in front of the box THROUGH Cloudflare — getting free wildcard SSL, anycast CDN, unlimited bandwidth, and DDoS protection — WITHOUT the box surrendering its standalone role. Concretely, bp cloud site deploy myblog --via cloudflare --domain blog.example.com: (a) writes/updates the DNS A record in the user's CF zone pointing blog.example.com at the box origin IP, flipped to PROXIED (orange cloud = the CDN/DDoS layer); (b) switches the box's Caddy to Origin-CA TLS mode so it STOPS on_demand ACME (which would 526 behind the proxy) and serves a long-lived CF Origin cert under Full(Strict); (c) the domain-status rung reports health honestly as :proxied (resolves to CF edge, origin reachable) instead of false-failing the standalone resolved==box check. Disconnect the provider → everything degrades back to pure standalone: :direct mode, on_demand TLS, box serves directly. Kinsta/Vercel bar: the verb STREAMS what it does ('writing DNS record… flipping to proxied… provisioning Origin CA… setting box TLS mode…'), fails CLOSED with an honest reason (no CF connected → clear message, never a crash), and degrades invisibly.

KEY CHOICES I LEAN TOWARD (tentative; Decide finalizes after two explore rounds): (1) Ship the DNS writer as CONTEXT-level orchestration on top of the merged Client callbacks — idempotent create-or-update by record name, proxied flag, delete on disconnect. (2) Add the small edge-binding migration D14 deferred; lean toward extending the site/barkpark row (custom_host precedent) over a new table UNLESS the survey shows a domain must bind independent of a site. Fields: the custom domain, zone_id (or CF-API discovery), serving_mode (:direct|:proxied), tls_mode/cert_path/key_path. (3) TLS: the Go renderer branch is landed — this wave WIRES it end-to-end (persist the mode, provision the Origin CA cert via the Client at expose-time, fix the two live-wiring caveats). At MINIMUM the mode must FLIP to origin-ca when CF-proxied so the box stops on_demand — the 526 fix is the load-bearing correctness gate (D18). (4) :proxied rung reads mode from the binding record, never the resolved IP; :direct byte-identical. (5) CLI: --via cloudflare on deploy + bp provider remove; no new noun. (6) Degrade proof mirrors plugin_free_boot_test — providers cleared, box still serves over its OWN TLS+DNS; assert configured?/0 fail-closed + SafeOutbound SSRF-guard on Real. (7) LIVE CF cutover = human gate (real CF account + a domain with NS delegated); scope the live proof to Fake-double integration + offline self-check, and file the cutover task clearly-marked.

PRIORITIZE / FINISH vs START: FINISH the end-to-end CF-in-front path connect→expose→DNS+TLS+status, degrade-proven — that is DNS writer + edge-binding migration + expose/--via + TLS end-to-end wiring + :proxied rung + degrade test. DEFER (already filed as backlog): Tunnel, R2, origin-health rung, subdomain-URL graduation. The edge capability fixture (D16) lands only if cheap. The single most load-bearing correctness gate is D18's 526-avoidance: a CF-proxied box MUST NOT run on_demand ACME. The single most load-bearing product gate is the standalone-degrade proof: with no CF connected, EVERYTHING works exactly as today.

(b) Origin CA auth is WRONG SCHEME, not a maybe: build_request/5 hardcodes 'Authorization: Bearer' for all 4 calls (real.ex:184-195), but POST /certificates needs X-Auth-User-Service-Key with a SEPARATE Origin CA Key — new credential slot + header branch + a CSR nothing in cloud/ or api/ generates.
